producer_report.summary: Per-kind check routing is built as routing.rs in athena-core, driven by per-check skip lists in athena.toml. It is called from the run path, and the docs and changelog are updated. In this send-back I changed no code. I reran `cargo test -p athena-core routing` and the full `cargo test --locked`, and both pass. The test `routing_follows_the_table_for_every_kind` checks all eight kinds against the section 3.2 table (checks run, checks skipped, whether a prior result may be reused, whether the workflow's own run is added). No speedup is measured, and the doc says so.

checks_run.note: run with --quiet; every test result line was ok, 0 failed

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core routing`: for each kind (code, tests, docs, design, config, build, study, other) the routed checks and skips match the section 3.2 table (docs, design and study skip fmt/clippy but always run test; config never skips; build adds the workflow's own run and never reuses a prior result).
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core routing` ran 11 tests, all passed. `routing_follows_the_table_for_every_kind` asserts runs, skips, reuse_prior and workflow_run for code, tests, docs, design, config, build, study and other against the committed athena.toml. Docs, design and study run only test and skip fmt and clippy. Config, code, tests and other run all three with no skips. Build runs all three, adds the workflow run and does not reuse a prior result. `routing_covers_every_kind_the_table_names` checks all eight kinds are recognised.

open_issues: I did not rerun fmt or clippy in this send-back round. They were run in the earlier round.
